review_type: AI visual comparison of native RGB removal smoke outputs
scope: Compared baseline, remove_car, remove_u, and remove_car_u native_rgb outputs for raw098/raw113/raw114 in native_strict_smoke_r1 and native_photo_smoke_r1. This is direct image review of native RGB renders, not semantic overlay review.
coordinate_convention: Approximate pixel regions in each 480x320 frame, origin upper-left. Bounding boxes describe image areas visually, not masks.

overall_findings.remove_car: The SUV body is largely replaced, but a dark, blurred, vehicle-shaped residue remains at its former location in all three frames. The lower part remains merged with a dark patch directly below the vehicle; the renders do not allow a confident split between residual body appearance and contact/projected shadow.
overall_findings.remove_u: The SUV remains visibly present, but its body is strongly corrupted by bright/colored artifacts. The artifact spills into nearby road/curb and toward the adjacent right-hand sedan. This is substantial change to both the target vehicle pixels and neighboring scene content; it is not a clean background-only edit.
overall_findings.remove_car_u: The car-shaped body is reduced, but a bright white/chromatic region and dark residual remain around its footprint. The corruption extends onto nearby roadway/curb pixels, visibly degrading the background in the removal area.
overall_findings.roadway: Outside the target region, baseline and remove_car preserve the major lane/cross-road markings and broad pavement texture more consistently. The combined remove_u outputs show the most obvious local background damage around and to the right of the SUV.
overall_findings.strict_vs_photo: Across the inspected 3 frames and four render variants, strict and photo smoke outputs look qualitatively near-identical. No clear visual gain from the photo-supported variant is apparent in these comparisons; subtle pixel-level differences are not assessed here.
overall_findings.expansion_recommendation: No current visual evidence justifies expanding either smoke variant to the full 49-frame run. The removal path still leaves a car-shaped dark residue, U-only editing damages the visible SUV and nearby background, combined removal leaves a bright halo, and strict versus photo shows no clear visual separation. First resolve what should happen to the dark footprint and validate preservation around the adjacent sedan/curb on targeted frames; then reassess expansion. This recommendation is limited to these three frames and is not a quantitative benchmark.

observations.baseline: The original dark SUV is visible in the center-right. The nearby light sedan is to its right.
observations.remove_car: A dark blurry, roughly car-shaped remnant remains around x=292..354, y=193..229. A darker horizontal area under it merges with the remnant, so separate body residue and shadow boundaries are uncertain.
observations.remove_u: The SUV remains but has bright saturated distortion across the body. A bright colored streak spills rightward across nearby roadway and reaches the vicinity/edge of the light sedan and curb.
observations.remove_car_u: The SUV shape is mostly suppressed, but a bright white/chromatic patch remains around x=286..364, y=185..230 with a darker lower remnant. Local pavement/curb and nearby right-side content are visibly altered.

frames.strict_vs_photo: No obvious difference in the viewed output images.

observations.baseline: The SUV is visible on the road. The white transverse road line lies farther below it and remains distinct.
observations.remove_car: A dark, low vehicle-shaped smear remains at approximately x=288..351, y=194..232. Its lower dark patch is contiguous with the blur; no clean projected-shadow edge is visible.
observations.remove_u: The SUV body is still present but heavily distorted by bright/color artifacts. The artifact affects the immediate road around the vehicle and streaks rightward toward the curb/adjacent vehicle area.
observations.remove_car_u: A bright blown-out/chromatic patch occupies the SUV footprint and spills to adjacent roadway/curb; dark residue is still visible at the bottom. The broad white transverse line below is not the main damaged area, but local pavement around the SUV is changed.

frames.strict_vs_photo: No clear visual quality difference in the inspected outputs.

observations.baseline: The dark SUV is visible, with the right-hand sedan partly cropped at the far right.
observations.remove_car: A dark blurred vehicle-like residue remains around x=288..350, y=198..234. A dark band immediately below merges with it and cannot be assigned separately to contact shadow.
observations.remove_u: The SUV remains visible but is strongly corrupted. Bright/color spill reaches the nearby pavement and curb to the right.
observations.remove_car_u: The vehicle body is mostly suppressed but replaced by bright white/chromatic contamination around the former footprint, with a dark lower residual. Nearby road/curb pixels are altered.

frames.strict_vs_photo: No obvious difference by direct visual inspection.

interpretation_limits: All judgments are AI model visual observations. No human ground-truth labels or physical shadow ownership labels are supplied.
A dark post-removal region cannot by itself establish that the remaining pixels are a real cast shadow; it may include residual vehicle appearance or rendering error.
The sample is three frames only. Visual similarity between strict and photo variants does not prove exact pixel equality or generalize to all 49 frames.
No GPU work was performed and no detection rule was edited.
